errors.text: The hypothesis makes the 400 K mechanism depend on a magnetically ordered C14 phase, although the C14-associated transition is near 214 K and the target does not require C14 long-range order at 400 K.

It relocates the principal Ti–Fe/Co/Ni antiferromagnetic coupling specifically to the fcc/C14 interface rather than treating antiparallel sublattice polarization as an electronic origin of reduced net magnetization.
It omits the requested spin-polarized electronic-structure calculation of the fcc density of states at the Fermi level.
It does not synthesize or measure the specified C14-dominant Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 comparator needed to assign the 214 K, 168 K, and 1084 K transitions by phase.
All cited evidence concerns unrelated alloy systems and does not support the claimed Ti magnetic coupling, FeCoNiTi phase assignments, or coercivity mechanism.
